queue.goal: Turn Relay's production primitives into a durable resumable operation framework so agents invoke policy-defined workflows instead of manually conducting every GitHub, Cloudflare, Runner and QA step.
queue.acceptance: Every substantial workflow can create a stable operation_id with persisted stage/state, exact source/head/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, timestamps, retry/reconciliation history, blocker/waiting-for-human state and recovery/rollback state; reconnecting agents can resume from the durable receipt without reconstructing chat history; server-side recipes cover at least ship-change, publish-worker, qa-then-merge and rollback-release; ambiguous mutations reconcile by readback before retry; event/webhook updates can advance operation state without chat polling; release policy supports bounded canary/verify/promote/rollback semantics without protection bypass; operation status/history is queryable for UI; tool-surface growth stays minimal by preferring recipes/resources/contracts over one tool per step.
queue.next_action: Define and test the operation/receipt schema and transition invariants first. Reuse existing Relay source/cloud/verify primitives; do not fork their auth or safety rules.

queue.goal: Make Relay's primary product experience an interactive in-chat MCP App rather than a prose wrapper around headless tools.
queue.acceptance: ChatGPT can render compact live operation cards, project status, release/deployment state and human-QA requests directly in conversation; human-QA UI consumes the canonical Runner QA-helper contract and Visuals IDs, supports targeted questions/checklists/notes/verdicts, and can expand into a full-screen review experience without creating a parallel store; render surfaces reuse durable Relay operation receipts and existing bounded mutation tools; headless production tools remain mostly headless; UI can send bounded follow-up actions/messages, refresh state, and preserve exact artifact identity; stale artifact/evidence state is visibly invalidated; mobile/desktop layouts remain useful; picture-in-picture/persistent mini-status may be explored where supported but is not required for correctness.
queue.next_action: Begin after the durable operation receipt shape is stable enough to consume. Treat the current qa-shell design as authoritative for human review interaction; wire to it rather than redesigning it.

queue.goal: Expose Relay's MCP App dashboard as a first-class authenticated web dashboard on relay.loew.fi with parity to the in-chat state model and controls.
queue.acceptance: relay.loew.fi presents the same projects, durable operations, publication receipts, QA handoffs, release state, recovery/rollback actions and history as the MCP App without duplicating state; shared components/data adapters are reused where practical; deep links can open a specific project/operation/release/QA item; auth and mutations use Relay's existing bounded control plane; web and in-chat surfaces remain behaviorally consistent; the dashboard consumes the future shared suite shell/navigation so Relay feels like one utility with Runner and Inspector rather than a separate website.
queue.next_action: Implement after the operation framework and core MCP App view-model/components are stable; do not create a second state or approval system for web.

queue.goal: Make inspector.loew.fi the suite's dedicated visual-review dashboard, moving the visual review experience out of Runner's product surface while keeping Runner as the coordination/evidence authority.
queue.acceptance: Inspector web renders screenshots, videos, live-preview availability, targeted QA-helper questions/checklists, notes/verdicts, upload/archive/expiry state and exact operation/publication context from Runner/Relay; Runner remains authoritative for Visuals receipts, QA identity and coordination rather than duplicating those stores in Inspector; Inspector supports direct links to exact evidence/run/artifact and full-screen review; Runner dashboard links/deep-links into Inspector for visual review instead of maintaining a competing review UI once migration is complete; the design consumes the shared suite shell and feels seamless with runner.loew.fi and relay.loew.fi; migration preserves historical review/evidence identity.
queue.next_action: Start only after Runner's current operator/qa-shell design and Visuals backend contracts settle enough to consume. Treat this as a presentation migration/integration, not an evidence-authority migration.
queue.reason: Shared Relay Review shipped in B4; standalone Inspector product retired in B6.

queue.goal: Ship Relay 1.8 as the contextual MCP experience and liveness release: ordinary Relay work should surface compact interactive cards for the relevant Runner, Inspector, Source and Cloud context, while every long-running operation exposes durable progress, heartbeat and stuck-state visibility so the user never has to guess whether a worker is still moving.
queue.acceptance: Canonical service/version metadata and release-facing UI/docs identify the resulting release as Relay 1.8.0. ChatGPT can render compact contextual cards for at least Runner project/assignment/preflight state, Source pull request/check/merge state, Cloud release/deployment state, Inspector evidence/review/human-QA state, and durable multi-step operations; cards preserve exact artifact/operation identity, refresh in place where the client supports it, and expand into the shared Relay app/fullscreen view instead of creating parallel mini-products. Cards clearly distinguish queued, working, waiting-on-external-system, waiting-for-human, blocked, stale/unresponsive, failed, rolled-back and complete states. Long-running active operations persist a meaningful heartbeat/updated_at plus human-readable current stage and next action at least every 10 minutes while work is genuinely progressing. By default, 20 minutes without a meaningful heartbeat/progress signal marks an active operation stale; the threshold may be configurable by operation class but must never silently extend itself. Crossing into blocked, failed, stale, waiting-for-human or complete emits one durable notification/attention event; repeated checks do not spam unless the state materially changes. If GitHub/Cloudflare/another dependency is still demonstrably running, Relay says so instead of falsely labeling the worker frozen; if the worker actually stopped heartbeating or hit quota/rate/auth/tool failure, Relay says that plainly and includes the last successful stage plus recovery action. Operation receipts persist stage/state, exact source/head/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, timestamps, retry/reconciliation history and waiting/blocker reasons so reconnecting clients can resume without chat history. Human-QA cards consume the existing Runner QA-helper/Visuals contracts and remain bound to exact evidence identity. Existing headless tools remain compatible; contextual UI is additive. Runner and Inspector retain the 1.7 identities/icons. Web and MCP surfaces use the same state model. Mobile/desktop layouts remain usable. Required tests, exact-head admission, MCP/web rendering checks and authenticated production readback pass before completion.
queue.next_action: Treat queued relay-operation-framework-20260930 and relay-mcp-app-ui-20260930 as prerequisite/source scope for this 1.8 release, not independent competing product directions. First stabilize the durable operation/receipt and progress-event model, including heartbeat/stale semantics and attention events; then bind contextual output templates/cards to existing Relay tools and the shared app, preserve 1.7 Runner/Inspector identity, validate exact-head behavior, ship as Relay 1.8.0, and leave a durable completion receipt.

queue.goal: Ship Relay 1.7.5 as an independently deployable observed-progress backend release that gives Relay one canonical, evidence-backed answer to 'what is actually happening right now?' before the 1.8 UI lands. Build the server-side progress/operation piping that 1.8 consumes; do not depend on or implement the 1.8 dashboard/card presentation.
queue.acceptance: Release-facing metadata identifies the backend release as Relay 1.7.5 and it can merge/deploy independently while relay-1.8-contextual-ui-20260930 continues on its separate UI-only scope. Introduce a canonical observed-progress model/receipt/event stream that reconciles Runner coordination state with concrete GitHub and Cloudflare evidence instead of treating claim state, next_action prose, lease presence, or declaration time as execution progress. Each tracked operation/assignment exposes a canonical stage, latest concrete progress event, last meaningful progress timestamp, worker heartbeat/freshness separately from external-system activity, exact known source/base/head/branch/PR/check/merge/version/deployment/runtime identities, waiting/blocker reason, and recovery action. The model must distinguish at least reserved-but-idle, working, waiting-on-external-system, waiting-for-human, blocked, possibly-stale, officially-stale/unresponsive, failed, rolled-back, and complete. A live GitHub/Cloudflare job must prevent false 'worker frozen' conclusions while still showing that the worker itself is waiting; a dead heartbeat, quota/rate/auth/tool failure must be represented plainly with last successful stage and recovery. Implement the 5-minute meaningful-heartbeat target, 10-minute possibly-stale evaluation, and 20-minute official-stale default as backend semantics/configurable policy, without silently extending stale thresholds. Persist durable progress events/receipts so reconnecting clients can reconstruct the timeline without chat history; repeated observations of unchanged state must not spam duplicate events. Add reconciliation logic for obvious coordination drift: completed/absorbed/superseded intent must be classifiable separately from live work, orphan/unregistered branches must be surfaced as reconciliation findings, and umbrella/held reservations must not be presented as active execution merely because they still occupy policy capacity. Expose a stable backwards-compatible MCP/API contract that 1.8 can consume for project/assignment/operation progress and recent events; existing 1.7 tools/clients continue to work. This release does not redesign dashboard/cards and must not write 1.8 UI files. Tests must cover Runner-only reserved state versus observed work, GitHub check/PR waits, Cloudflare deploy waits, heartbeat freshness, stale transitions, deduped events, exact identity propagation, drift/reconciliation classification, and 1.8 consumer contract shape. Required install/tests, exact-head admission, merge, exact-source deployment, runtime readback and durable completion receipt must pass.
queue.next_action: Claim this as soon as a branch slot is legitimately available, without taking over or folding into the active 1.8 branch. Implement the canonical progress schema/event receipt first, then evidence adapters/reconciliation for Runner + GitHub + Cloudflare, then expose the stable consumer API/tool contract. Keep all UI rendering in 1.8. Before completion, leave a precise consumer handoff in docs/relay/RELAY_1_7_5_RELEASE.md describing the fields/events 1.8 must bind to and explicitly stating that UI must not infer progress from claim state or next_action prose.

queue.goal: Ship Relay 1.9 as the skills-runtime and creative-intelligence release: add a first-class relay.SKILLS system that discovers, validates, versions, resolves and loads portable expertise on demand, then use it to make Relay substantially stronger at aesthetic direction, interaction/flow, motion, platform-native UI craft and performance across web, macOS, Windows, Android and Linux/GNOME while expanding its engineering, GitHub and Cloudflare expertise without bloating the permanent MCP/tool surface.
queue.acceptance: Release-facing metadata/docs identify Relay 1.9.0. Introduce a first-class skills registry/runtime with stable catalog/search/read/resolve/install-or-vendor/update/audit behavior and a manifest that records id/name/version/source, Relay-authored vs licensed-upstream vs private-project origin, license/provenance/source URL or repository+revision, integrity/hash, tags, dependencies, required/optional MCP capabilities, supported platforms, compatibility and update policy. Portable SKILL.md bundles may include references/scripts/assets, but untrusted executable content never gains ambient authority; validation, path containment, size/context budgets and dependency/capability checks fail closed. Skills are selected and loaded just-in-time from task intent/capability requirements rather than injected wholesale; resolution is deterministic/explainable and can report why a skill was chosen, rejected or unavailable. Add an upstream ingestion policy/pipeline that license-audits and pins redistributable skills instead of copying proprietary installed skills; preserve attribution and make update drift auditable. Creative priority packs cover aesthetic/art direction and anti-slop judgment, information architecture and interaction flow, design systems/tokens/components, motion/animation/microinteraction, visual-reference analysis and visual QA, plus platform-native guidance for web, macOS/SwiftUI, Windows/WinUI, Android/Material and Linux/GNOME/GTK/libadwaita. Figma-bound skills may orchestrate the real Figma MCP when present but must declare that dependency and degrade cleanly when absent; Relay does not counterfeit external tools. Performance/optimization is co-equal with creative quality: packs cover asset/image/font budgets, animation/compositor discipline, JS/CSS/runtime cost, rendering/hydration, network/cache/CDN strategy, Core Web Vitals or platform-equivalent profiling, and performance-aware visual effects; aesthetically ambitious output must carry explicit performance checks/budgets rather than disabling effects by default. Supporting packs cover build/frontend engineering, research/source-driven development, documentation, release engineering, testing/QA, accessibility and security; these are lower product priority for the current solo workflow but must provide a safe production baseline and be composable with creative packs. Expand GitHub skills around branch/PR/check/release/repository workflows and Cloudflare skills around Workers, builds/deployments, bindings, Access, cache/CDN/R2/browser/evidence flows, always reusing Relay's bounded SOURCE/CLOUD mutation primitives and exact-head/readback safety rather than bypassing them. Provide project-private skill overlays so Terra Prime/Field/other loew doctrine can extend general skills without forking upstream bundles. Add tests for manifest validation, provenance/license policy, deterministic resolution, JIT context limits, dependency/tool gating, hostile/pathological bundles, update/version drift and representative cross-pack composition. Existing Relay 1.8 contextual UI/progress contracts remain compatible. No giant prompt dump, no one-tool-per-skill explosion, no new standing credentials. Required install/tests, exact-head admission, release verification and durable 1.9 completion receipt must pass.
queue.next_action: Begin only after Relay 1.8 is merged or its skill-facing contracts are stable enough not to collide. Phase A: specify the skill manifest, provenance/license model, trust boundaries, resolver and JIT context budget. Phase B: implement registry/read/resolve/audit with a tiny MCP surface and representative fixture skills. Phase C: seed the high-priority Creative pack (aesthetic, flow, motion, visual QA, performance) plus platform adapters for web/macOS/Windows/Android/GNOME and Figma dependency bindings. Phase D: add build/research/docs/release/testing/accessibility/security plus GitHub and Cloudflare operational packs. Phase E: add upstream import/update auditing, project-private overlays, cross-pack composition tests, docs and 1.9 release verification. Treat public upstream candidates such as Impeccable/MengTo-style design skill libraries only as candidates until their exact license/provenance is verified at import time.
